free_tier.stated: No free tier. The vendor states compute nodes start at EUR 1 per month; the entry rung's shape is not shown on any first-party page reached. A tracker lists a Node 2GB at EUR 3.00 a month for 1 core, 2 GB, 20 GB SSD and 2 TB traffic.

retention.stated: the vendor's deploy page lists monthly prices with a struck-through higher figure beside each; no deletion grace period is printed

egress.terms: not published on the pages reached; a tracker lists 2 TB for the Node 2GB

interface_detail: KVM guests with a dedicated /64 IPv6 subnet and no IPv4; the vendor preconfigures a DNS64/NAT64 resolver so the guest can still reach IPv4-only destinations outbound. A free reverse proxy gives any domain a dual-stack HTTP endpoint.
tooling: any SSH client over IPv6; the control panel is cloud.v6node.com and is behind a login
chaining: the only row whose IPv4 problem is solved for outbound traffic by design (DNS64/NAT64) rather than by an add-on, which makes it the best fit for a monitor that has to poll IPv4-only targets

limits.value: not published on the pages reached; 2 TB per a tracker row for the Node 2GB
one dedicated /64 per node; no IPv4 address, and NAT64 covers outbound only

binding_note: no IPv4 at all and NAT64 is outbound-only, so nothing on the IPv4 internet can open a connection to the guest unless it goes through the reverse proxy.

identity_cost.detail: an account on cloud.v6node.com, which returned a login wall to every read attempt. The vendor states payment by 'Apple/ Google Pay, all major credit/debit cards and SEPA direct debit', so a debit card is explicitly accepted. No card hold is stated.

reliability_note: no reliability event observed; a 2022 LowEndBox offer for the same provider advertised 4.5 EUR a year, so the entry price has risen since
confidence_note: the EUR 1 entry price, the IPv6-only statement, the DNS64/NAT64 statement, the /64 and the payment rails are quoted from first-party pages today, but the entry rung's shape and traffic allowance are not published on any page reached, and the control panel is login-walled. The shape in this record is a tracker's, not the vendor's.

notes: The architecture is the most useful of the IPv6-only hosts, and the price is the least documented. DNS64/NAT64 is the answer to the caveat that governs every other row here: a guest on this host can reach IPv4-only destinations outbound without buying an IPv4 address, which is exactly what a health monitor polling IPv4 endpoints needs. What could not be established is what EUR 1 actually buys: the marketing site says 'starting at €1 per month', the deploy page starts at EUR 4.49, and the only shape figure is a tracker's Node 2GB at EUR 3.00. The control panel is login-walled, so the entry rung's RAM, disk and traffic are unverified. The entity is a sole trader with a German VAT ID, which is a weaker counterparty than a GmbH but is a real registered taxpayer.
